report.source_text: The patient was referred to the Department of Clinical Dermatology with initial treatment of 5 mg prednisone twice daily. After DIF results, a definitive diagnosis of PV was obtained, and 40 mg of systemic prednisone was prescribed along with nystatin antifungal (100000 per 3 mL) mouthwash. A week later, the dose was increased to 60 mg daily with continued use of nystatin mouthwash. After two weeks of the continued use of systemic prednisone, a significant improvement was seen, followed by a period of maintenance where the dose decreased gradually down to 5 mg daily (Figures 7, 8).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 42-year-old male presented with a two-month history of diffuse oral ulceration and skin lesions, dysphagia, dehydration, and severe weight loss, with prior corticosteroid treatment failure. Clinical examination revealed erythema multiforme-like symptoms extraorally and diffuse ragged erosions intraorally. Oral mucosal biopsy showed acantholysis and suprabasal clefting on histopathology. Direct immunofluorescence (DIF) confirmed intercellular IgG and C3 in a mesh-like pattern, with C3 restricted to the basal and suprabasal cell layer, leading to a definitive diagnosis of Pemphigus Vulgaris. Treatment with systemic prednisone resulted in significant improvement.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with diffuse ulceration on the oral cavity involving the tongue, floor of the mouth, buccal mucosa, lips, and palate, in addition to skin lesions, dysphagia, dehydration, and severe weight loss, with relapse and recurrence despite prior corticosteroid treatment.
Extraoral examination showed erythema multiforme-like symptoms including crusting ulceration on the lips and nasal sill.
Intraorally, desquamative gingivitis and diffuse ragged erosions were haphazardly distributed on the buccal mucosa, tongue, palate, and floor of the mouth.
Oral mucosal biopsy histopathology showed nonkeratinized stratified squamous with acantholysis and suprabasal clefting, 'row of tombstones', and mild inflammatory infiltrate.
Direct immunofluorescence (DIF) showed intercellular immunoglobulin (Ig) G and C3 on a mesh-like pattern, with C3 restricted to the basal and suprabasal cell layer.
Treatment with systemic prednisone (starting at 40mg, increased to 60mg daily) along with nystatin mouthwash led to significant improvement.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.alternative: Other blistering diseases (e.g., Bullous Pemphigoid, Mucous Membrane Pemphigoid)
ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: The specific histopathological finding of acantholysis and suprabasal clefting (E002) combined with the highly characteristic direct immunofluorescence pattern of intercellular IgG and C3 (E003) strongly supports Pemphigus Vulgaris over other blistering conditions.
While EM-like symptoms were noted extraorally (E001), the histopathology (E002) and DIF findings (E003) are not consistent with Erythema Multiforme as the primary diagnosis.
